questions.label: Next-phase outcomes
questions.q: Now that Fusion ERP is implemented, what would you most like the next phase to deliver for the business?

questions.up: A concrete adoption, close, efficiency or decision-making outcome makes the corresponding customer lessons more useful.
questions.down: Broad product overviews that do not help that outcome.
questions.follow: What would make you say the conference was time well spent?

questions.label: Maturity dimensions
questions.q: Which parts of Fusion maturity would you most like to advance next?
questions.why: Distinguishes feature use, people and skills, process performance, governance and platform operations.
questions.up: Adoption examples for enablement; release models for continuous change; data practices for reliable decisions.
questions.down: Sessions about dimensions his team does not want to advance now.
questions.follow: If you can share the maturity snapshot you referenced, which findings should guide our choices?

questions.label: Time horizon
questions.q: Are you looking for actions the team can take soon, a longer-term roadmap, or a mix of both?
questions.why: Balances practical methods and workshops with strategic product direction; it does not establish feature availability.
questions.up: LRN2365 and adoption planning for an actionable backlog; LRN1613 and LRN1763 for longer-term direction.
questions.down: Roadmap-heavy content if he needs immediate operating practices, or detailed labs if he needs strategy.
questions.follow: What decision would you like the team to make after the conference?

questions.label: Build on existing work

questions.up: Customer lessons that extend his current adoption, governance, support or release practices.
questions.down: Introductory material covering methods his team already uses successfully.
questions.follow: Is there an approach you would particularly like to compare with peers?

questions.label: Data practices
questions.q: Which ongoing data-quality or governance decisions would you like customer examples to help with?
questions.why: Separates finance hierarchies, operational records, controls, stewardship and reporting reliability without assuming a deficiency.
questions.up: Experian/EDM for finance structures; Tallgrass for operating controls; Meta/Wipro for standards and ownership.
questions.down: Data-product sessions outside the relevant domain; none is presented as a Syniti session.
questions.follow: What would you like to see made more repeatable or easier to measure?

questions.label: Connected data
questions.q: Should the data sessions focus mainly on Fusion, or on how finance data stays reliable across connected systems?
questions.why: Sets the scope for integration, reconciliation, observability and producer-to-consumer accountability.
questions.up: Arlington, Cigna and Snapchat for connected data; Fusion observability and shared metrics where relevant.
questions.down: Architecture-heavy cross-platform content if the question is ownership inside Fusion.
questions.follow: Which handoff or type of reconciliation would make a useful example, without getting into confidential design details?

questions.label: Release execution
questions.q: Which part of your quarterly release approach would you most like to compare with other customers?
questions.why: Distinguishes impact assessment, opt-in decisions, testing, communication and rollout ownership.
questions.up: Cummins for the adoption gap; Polk County for triage; Tennessee and DocuSign for collaboration; QA sessions for validation.
questions.down: Deep testing tools if decision-making or user readiness is the greater need.
questions.follow: Would a peer walkthrough of one release cycle be more helpful than a tool demonstration?

questions.label: Redwood
questions.q: What would you like to bring back about Redwood adoption?
questions.why: Clarifies the desired planning lesson without assuming Comcast has or has not adopted Redwood.
questions.up: Milwaukee Tool for readiness and customization evaluation; cross-pillar customer lessons and UX direction as supporting context.
questions.down: General UX vision if the need is detailed rollout execution; that gap stays explicit.
questions.follow: Would readiness, dependencies, phased rollout or user enablement be the most useful part to explore?

questions.label: Comparable peers
questions.q: What would make another customer’s experience comparable enough to be useful?
questions.why: Avoids equating a recognizable logo or industry match with the same operating complexity.
questions.up: Mayo for disclosed employee scale; McDonald’s/global finance, CHS/shared services, Hearst/media and AT&T/communications as appropriate.
questions.down: Examples whose stage, footprint or operating model does not answer his question.
questions.follow: Does scale, global footprint, finance complexity, maturity or operating model matter most?

questions.label: Service experience
questions.q: What would you most like to learn from customers working with CSS, TAM or MCS?
questions.why: Turns a connection request into a useful learning objective without assuming service usage or a purchase initiative.
questions.up: Explicit Oracle Customer Success Services sessions for value realization, responsibilities, adoption and innovation.
questions.down: Infrastructure-led examples if the desired lesson is application operations; no session is labeled TAM/MCS without evidence.
questions.follow: Would the most useful conversation be about day-to-day ownership, specialist support, adoption or measuring value?

questions.label: Attendance and depth
questions.q: Which conference days and existing commitments should we plan around, and what balance of customer discussions, practical sessions and hands-on learning would suit you?
questions.why: Makes a realistic four-day plan possible and prevents paid all-day training or long labs from crowding out higher-value learning.
questions.up: A single suitable offering of repeated labs, peer exchange and focused customer sessions that fit confirmed attendance.
questions.down: Unavailable days, duplicate learning objectives and paid training without confirmed interest.
questions.follow: Would you like us to reserve open time for expert or peer conversations that still need coordination?

paths.title: Define the next phase of ERP value
paths.answer: I want a defensible view of what to improve next and how to measure it.
paths.limit: Compare customer sequencing and frameworks with the maturity snapshot when supplied. No maturity level or 90-day commitment is assigned here.

paths.title: Sustain adoption and advance Fusion maturity
paths.answer: The next phase should turn deployed capabilities into everyday use.
paths.limit: Choose a learning and feedback operating model. Oracle University addresses skills and certification preparation; no complete certification curriculum is established by the catalog.

paths.title: Build a repeatable finance AI operating model
paths.answer: I need clearer ownership, governance, skills and measures as AI expands.
paths.limit: Oracle Finance provides a customer-zero view; Howmet is an HR example. Compare transferability rather than assuming a matching Finance AI Center of Excellence.

paths.title: Find proven finance AI value
paths.answer: I want specific customer use cases and evidence of business benefit.
paths.limit: Prioritize named customer outcomes. Separate reported results, current deployment, readiness work and planned capabilities; none predicts Comcast’s results.

paths.title: Focus on faster close and accounting operations
paths.answer: Close readiness and less manual accounting work are the most useful outcomes.
paths.limit: EPM close and Fusion ERP accounting are different scopes. Confirm which systems and processes belong in Josh’s learning plan before choosing a lab or demonstration.

paths.title: Improve data quality and accountability
paths.answer: I want stronger, sustainable finance data practices and clearer ownership.
paths.limit: Finance structures, risk controls and broader standards address different domains. No Syniti-specific session was confirmed, and EDM is not a universal replacement for governance practices.

paths.title: Manage data across connected systems
paths.answer: The important question is how data remains trustworthy across finance boundaries.
paths.limit: Compare freshness, observability, shared definitions and operating responsibilities. The catalog does not provide one complete producer-to-consumer stewardship or reconciliation playbook.

paths.title: Make release execution more deliberate
paths.answer: I want to compare change assessment, feature decisions, testing and communication.
paths.limit: Select by the specific release question. TFG’s quantified testing example is HCM; LRN2263 is EPM. Security updates and SaaS patch responsibilities are not established by a general QA session.

paths.title: Plan Redwood adoption
paths.answer: I want readiness and rollout lessons for Redwood.
paths.limit: Milwaukee Tool describes planned adoption; HBL is HCM; UX direction is supporting context. A finance-specific opt-in/dependency/phased-rollout checklist was not confirmed.

paths.title: Learn from comparable customers
paths.answer: I want examples with a useful match in scale, complexity or operating model.
paths.limit: The site shows only disclosed scale and context. The peer exchange is a verified group opportunity, not a guarantee of specific attendees or private access.

paths.title: Understand service-supported customer experience
paths.answer: I want to understand how customer and service teams sustain value after implementation.
paths.limit: These entries explicitly name Oracle Customer Success Services. TAM/MCS usage and matching contract or support scope were not confirmed. Tailored introductions need separate account-team/CSS coordination.

paths.title: Explore capabilities after the customer lessons
paths.answer: I want to connect peer practices to the product’s future direction or try a bounded use case.
paths.limit: Roadmaps, demonstrations and labs support evaluation; they do not establish production availability, prerequisites met, or a business case. Sunday university training is paid where the catalog says so.

context: Fusion ERP implementation is complete. The next phase and maturity level remain to be clarified; the referenced maturity snapshot has not been supplied.
